sector: Consumer Discretionary (Recreational Boat & Yacht Retail / Marina Operations)
drawdown_context: HZO peaked ~$87 in 2021 and traded ~$30 in November 2024 around the FY24 10-K filing date; by April 2025 (Q2 10-Q filing) stock had fallen to ~$23 (Q2 ASR purchases at $23.15). HZO carries ~$710M floor plan + $356M LT debt against equity of $986M and inventory of $907M with rising aging risk. Drawdown is driven by demand destruction in luxury boat/yacht discretionary, hurricane impacts in Florida (51-53% of dealership revenue), AND the IGY acquisition leverage residue. The forensic question is whether the company is honestly representing covenant headroom and goodwill durability.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of September 30, 2024, we were in compliance with all of the covenants under the Amended Credit Agreement and our additional available borrowings under the Amended Credit Agreement was approximately $1.5 million based upon the outstanding borrowing base availability.' Floor Plan outstanding $709.0M against a $950M facility. Covenants: leverage ratio not to exceed 3.35 to 1.0; consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio greater than 1.10 to 1.0. The 10-K MD&A states 'we believe that the cash generated from sales and our existing capital resources will be adequate to meet our liquidity and capital requirements for at least the next 12 months.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: Test the gap between technical compliance and effective borrowing headroom. With $1.5M of $950M floor plan (0.16%) free, the binding constraint is the BORROWING BASE (aging-curtailment-driven advance rate) not the covenant. The 12-month sufficiency claim should be tested against ACTUAL operating cash flow and inventory growth, not the stated covenant compliance.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 operating cash flow: NEGATIVE $25.7M (vs negative $222.2M FY23, positive $76.6M FY22). Floor Plan grew from $537.1M (FY23) to $709.0M (FY24) = +$171.9M. Cash $224M (FY24) vs $201M (FY23). Inventory $906.6M (FY24) vs $812.8M (FY23) up $94M. Available borrowings: $1.5M floor plan + ~$86M revolver + $100M draw mortgage. The aging-curtailment provision in the credit agreement REDUCES the allowable advance rate as inventory ages so a soft-retail / aging-inventory scenario is a borrowing-base squeeze (NOT a covenant trip) that automatically tightens at the worst moment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Technical covenant compliance (Mode A passes) but the effective floor-plan cushion is $1.5M functionally zero and the curtailment mechanic means inventory aging directly compresses borrowing capacity. The '12-month liquidity sufficient' framing depends on a Floor Plan that has expanded $172M in FY24 and is now $1.5M from its borrowing-base ceiling, while operating cash flow turned negative. This is a structurally fragile setup that the optimistic MD&A 'liquidity sufficient' framing materially understates.

Test whether the substantive terms (covenant relief, accordion, pricing, advance rate changes) match the MD&A 12-month sufficiency narrative.

rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K filed 2024-11-14 references most recent amendment as Third Amendment (March 27, 2024). Q1 10-Q filed 2025-01-23 introduces Fourth Amendment (Oct 29, 2024) as Exhibit 10.1 without any narrative description in MD&A or footnote text. Q1 10-Q covenants remain identical to 10-K (leverage 3.35x, FCCR 1.10x) and Floor Plan limit unchanged at $950M. So either: (a) the Fourth Amendment is a non-material technical modification (then why filed as a material exhibit?), or (b) it materially changed advance rates, pricing, or covenant calculation methodology in a way not narrated. Either way, the 10-K omitted a material subsequent event from a Nov 14 filing 16 days after the amendment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Filing a Fourth Amendment to a $1.4B-aggregate credit facility two weeks before the 10-K, with zero narrative disclosure in the 10-K, is the canonical forensic 'thing not said' pattern Mode B is designed to catch. Even if the Fourth Amendment is benign, the choice not to disclose it while presenting a 12-month-sufficient narrative violates the spirit of subsequent-event reporting. Combined with the $1.5M floor-plan cushion, this is consistent with covenant relief or borrowing-base recalibration that management would not want to highlight.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: A qualitative-only goodwill assessment in a fiscal year with operating income down 36%, net income down 65%, operating cash flow negative, AND internal earnout projections assuming 23-25% NOI growth is a forensic mismatch. The earnout projection (which DROVE the contingent-consideration MARK-DOWN booked later see C5) is implicitly the same forecast supporting goodwill carrying value. The audit committee may have accepted qualitative-only, but if the earnout marks-down (which they materially DID in Q1 FY25), the same downward revision should pressure-test goodwill at the FY25 annual test.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K contingent consideration: $86.1M opening balance (FY23) -> additions $1.3M -> settlements ($3.0M) -> mark-to-market change ($3.0M reduction) -> $81.3M ending balance. Discount rate disclosure: 11.0%, earnout projected growth 23%-25%. Q2 FY25 10-Q (filed April 24, 2025): contingent consideration plummets to $4.9M (from $81.3M) a $76.4M reduction in 6 months. Q1 10-Q cash flow shows '$25.7M change in fair value of contingent consideration' as a NON-CASH benefit running through SG&A. Discount rate in Q2 10-Q: '11%-17%' (range materially widened).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: Contingent consideration mark-down forensics. A $76.4M contingent-consideration reduction over 6 months means either (a) sellers got paid out ($51M of cash settlements is plausible), or (b) acquired-entity earnout targets are now expected to be massively missed (mark-to-market reduction). The SG&A benefit ($25.7M Q1 alone) artificially flatters Q1 'cost control' narrative. The discount rate range widening to 17% signals higher uncertainty about whether targets will be hit.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 SG&A: $130.7M vs $156.5M prior-year Q1 = $25.8M decrease. Cash flow statement attributes 'changes in fair value of contingent consideration' of $25.7M (NON-CASH) to that SG&A line. So organic SG&A was essentially FLAT YoY despite revenue down 11.2% a deteriorating cost-revenue ratio that the headline SG&A 'decrease' obscures. Q2 10-Q discount rate widened to 11%-17% (from 11% flat at FY24-end), and total contingent consideration crashed from $81.3M to $4.9M implying acquired-entity earnout targets are now expected to be largely missed. This is the same forecasting infrastructure that supports goodwill carrying value (C3).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two compounding tells: (1) Q1 SG&A 'cost discipline' narrative ($-25.8M YoY) is almost entirely a non-cash mark-to-market benefit, not operating leverage quality of earnings is poor. (2) The contingent-consideration mark-down implies acquired entities (IGY, AGY, Williams, Native Marine, etc.) are missing earnout targets which means the same growth assumptions used to AVOID a quantitative goodwill test (C3) are demonstrably impaired. The mismatch between 'we performed qualitative only' and 'we marked down $76M of earnout liabilities for those same entities' is forensic-grade inconsistency.

With Q1 FY25 SSS at -11%, building inventory $66.8M from Sep 30, 2024 to Mar 31, 2025 (+7%) and floor plan +$112.7M (+16%) implies aged inventory accumulation. Floor plan grew $284M in 18 months against essentially flat available borrowings ($1.5-4M), indicating the lender is keeping HZO at the edge of the borrowing base. The aging curtailment mechanic means a Spring/Summer 2025 boat-show season miss would compress borrowing base AT THE PEAK INVENTORY MONTH. Late-cycle tariff cost layer is not yet quantified. This is the highest-probability covenant-or-base-default path.

summary: HZO is a TECHNICALLY-COMPLIANT-BUT-FRAGILE marine-retail roll-up with five reinforcing forensic tells: (1) Floor Plan at $821.7M outstanding with $4M of borrowing-base headroom (Q2 FY25), where the aging-curtailment mechanic automatically tightens at the worst moment; (2) a Fourth Amendment to the credit agreement (Oct 29, 2024) was filed as a Q1 10-Q exhibit but is NOT disclosed anywhere in the 10-K signed two weeks later a material subsequent-event omission; (3) contingent consideration collapsed $76.4M from $81.3M to $4.9M in 6 months with $25.7M of that running through SG&A as a non-cash benefit that artificially flatters Q1 'cost discipline,' and the discount rate widened from 11% to 11%-17% signaling acquired-entity earnouts are now expected to be missed the same forecasts that support the $592M goodwill carrying value (60% of equity); (4) the FY24 10-K, signed 45 days into Q1 FY25 with hurricanes Helene/Milton already past, gives no forward warning for the -11% Q1 SSS print that arrives 10 weeks later; (5) the company is buying back $12.4M of stock in March 2025 while operating cash flow is -$73.6M H1 FY25 and floor plan is $4M from its ceiling all funded out of credit-facility expansion. Offsetting positives: long-tenured KPMG auditor (since 2013), long-tenured CFO McLamb (since 1998), no Item 9 disagreements, no going-concern, no ICFR weakness, CAM is sector-appropriate (trade-in fair value). NET: a MODERATE SHORT-tier signal the governance signals are clean enough to avoid full RED FLAG NEGATIVE territory, but the combination of borrowing-base fragility, undisclosed amendment, low-quality earnings (contingent-consideration mark-down running through SG&A), and forward demand softness against goodwill that depends on earnouts being missed is a coherent forensic pattern that the honesty-alpha framework should de-rate.
